captions.fig2_sparse_vs_dense: Figure 2: For the same TF-IDF numbers, CSR storage needs 54x less memory than a dense array (14 MB vs 763 MB at 20K docs) and our inverted-index sparse-sparse kernel is 81x faster than single-threaded BLAS dense-dense and 6x faster than scoring 768-d embeddings; we still choose dense embeddings (59 MB) because they rank the correct abstract first more often (hit@1 74% vs 68%; hit@10 90% vs 90%) and match paraphrased queries that share no keywords with the documents.
captions.fig2b_density_crossover: Figure 2b: Sparse storage only pays off for very sparse data: with single-threaded kernels, BLAS dense-dense overtakes our sparse kernel at about 20% density, while our TF-IDF matrix is 0.92% dense.
